topic: Low findings of the SP-076 security audit
detail: (1) Paths, roots and patterns compare by Go's strings.ToLower text, not as APFS compares names (Unicode NFC/NFD, full case folding): a source registered under another spelling of a private root's folder could miss that root and, under a '~/code/**' pattern, be placed public. The text comparison predates SP-076 but SP-076 makes it reachable; a fix needs Unicode normalization (golang.org/x/text, a new dependency) or an os.SameFile check against stricter roots. Not tested on disk. (2) An agent's ExplainPlacement answers only for public_path matches, so it can confirm a guessed folder name in a literal pattern even though the pattern is never shown; mitigations: refuse non-existent paths for agents, or rate-limit per caller. (3) Patterns are case-insensitive, so on a case-sensitive volume '~/code/oss' also matches a session-created '~/code/OSS'.
